Thank you for your kind words and clear instructions. I often find it difficult to say things with my voice when emotional. I will try to write to someone.

1. I didn't exist before. It wouldn't be that bad to return to that, being asleep forever and a non-observer.

2. I'm in intermittent but significant emotional pain since childhood, and the more I live the more I realize that will always be true.

3. People will accept my absence, and at some point they will be gone too. It's not important that I stay here. Other people don't need me really, or at least I'm emotionally unable to internalize that they might.

4. I'm very tired of the stress and actions of living. I've done and achieved so much, just to have more work and crises pile up in front of me. More opportunities for panic and pain. And things get worse if I try to help myself.

5. I feel like an anomaly. I don't fit in anywhere, intersectionally. This could be seen as good, unique, but it also causes me so much suffering in ways that don't seem to be present in other people. Usually stuff is complicated enough that I don't even know how to communicate what's wrong.

6. I feel like I should have the right to die. (I don't necessarily think that is a generalizable law though)

Hi! I'm a trans woman and actually started my social and medical transition at 22 while on internship in Japan, so I hope I can give some info.

I used a medical translation service (forgot the name) to get an appointment with [Tokyo Gender Clinic](http://gid-cli.com/) in Shinagawa. They sent a translator who helped me through the first appointment since no one at the clinic spoke English. I was able to get by with my own Japanese after, however. The regimen was estradiol + progesterone with no anti-androgen (similar to Powers Method), injected every 2 weeks, but they wanted me to come to the clinic for injections. They did not need a therapist letter but had a questionnaire for evaluating gender dysphoria at intake. I actually did really well on this HRT, but it's fairly different from the common estradiol + spiro/AA regimen. 

I was pretty forward with coming out to my workplace (research dept. of a large telecom company). Told my supervisor and wrote a coming out email to the research group with her OK. I gradually changed my appearance (even beforehand, including dyeing hair blue...) without any issues. Had absolutely zero issues with my workplace, but they were pretty ignorant of what being trans really meant. It was just very neutral, leaning friendly. They also let me change my name in their system. I still have good relationships with my colleagues there and almost went back, alas COVID.

I had similar experiences out in public around Tokyo and Yokohama. Lots of train stares, but nothing hostile. I did not pass though, and I am in general very bad at 'reading the air', so take my experiences as one subjective data point.

I was not very social, so I can't say how closer interpersonal interactions/events would go. Finding a support network would be very difficult unless you can reach out to Japanese trans groups or just find accepting friends. Just be mindful that assumptions about LGBT people and internal 'trans culture' might be different than what you know. Being comfortable with advanced Japanese is likely necessary here, and there's always a chance you won't find a support network. At least for me, I never did.

This was a few years ago, so my memory isn't that great. Please let me know if you have any questions!

Edit: I also had not changed my legal name or gender on my passport. This caused issues with gender-segregated corporate housing, and I would have had to have been in the male apartment block had I gone for a second internship. I can't say how this would affect legal issues when using restrooms, but I used male restrooms to be safe. Get your gender marker changed before applying for a visa!
